newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says sold more petroleum products Jan-Apr.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says sold more petroleum products Jan-Apr.

text.p: Mexican sales of petroleum products rose by three percent in the first four months of the year compared with the same period in 1996, Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) chairman Adrian Lajous said on Monday.
Lajous said the sale of petroleum products averaged 1.778 million barrels per day (bpd), and that natural gas and fuel oil sales had risen as well.
The head of the state oil and gas monopoly spoke to reporters after a meeting with local businessmen.
The Pemex chairman travelled to this northern industrial city to talk with glass, plastic and ceramic makers, who have complained about the volatility of natural gas prices.

Lajous said he assured the companies that natural gas and fuel oil prices have fallen since a seasonal peak in prices in the winter months. Pemex has been studying ways to control volatility in fuel costs.
